title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the primary reference for employees, managers, and approvers. For team-level variations (e.g., SRE runbooks, product-specific procurements), follow the linked team pages.

Scope and governance

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Owner: People Ops (document owner)
- Review cadence: annual or after a significant incident or regulatory change
- Escalation path: People Ops -> Legal -> Security -> CEO (for policy exceptions)

1) Access & permissions

Principles
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimal permissions required for business tasks.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default for services that support it.
- Time-limited access: temporary elevated access must be approved and logged.

Process
1. Access request: submit via the Access Request template (see 'Internal templates').
2. Manager approval: manager confirms business justification within 3 business days.
3. Owner approval: the resource owner (service or data owner) approves or denies within 3 business days.
4. Access provisioning: IT/Security or the owning team provisions access and documents the change in the access log.
5. Review: quarterly access reviews for privileged groups.

RBAC matrix (summary)
| Role | Typical members | Approver | Review cadence |
|------|-----------------|----------|----------------|
| Read-only | Contractors, analysts | Team lead | Quarterly |
| Developer | Engineers | Service owner | Quarterly |
| Admin/Privileged | SRE, Platform | Security lead | Monthly |

Temporary access
- Max duration: 14 days by default. Extensions require re-approval by the manager + owner.
- Emergency access: request via on-call SRE and recorded in incident ticket; post-facto review required within 72 hours.

Owner and contacts
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (RBAC & provisioning): security-team@redwood.com

2) Change management

Scope
- Applies to production changes to services, infra, config that affect availability, reliability, or data integrity (includes model deployments, schema changes, infra changes).

Change categories and approval matrix
- Standard change: pre-approved routine changes with documented rollback and runbook (no additional approvals required).
- Normal change: requires manager + change board (Change Advisory Board) approval. Plan must include roll back and load testing results.
- Emergency change: implemented immediately with post-implementation review within 72 hours.

Process (Normal change)
1. Create a Change Request (CR) using the Change Request template. Include owner, impact assessment, rollback plan, test plan, and scheduled window.
2. Submit CR to Change Board at least 48 hours before the planned window.
3. Change Board evaluates risk, impact, and schedules approval. Approvals expected within 24 business hours.
4. Implement change during approved window with monitoring and a dedicated rollback procedure.
5. Post-change validation and an entry in the change log.

Emergency changes
- Notify on-call and the Change Board immediately.
- Implement temporary fix if required to restore service.
- Document all actions and complete a Post-Change Review within 72 hours.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Regular change window: Tue/Wed 02:00-04:00 UTC (team-specific exceptions must be documented).
- Blackout: major release periods (noted on the company release calendar).

3) Data management

Data classification
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: for internal business use; low risk if exposed but not publicized.
- Confidential: contains PII, customer data, or IP; requires encryption at rest & in transit.
- Restricted: legal, regulated, or contractual datasets with strict processing/retention rules.

Storage and handling
- Confidential and Restricted data require encryption (AES-256 or equiv) at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit.
- Do not store customer PII in free-text logs. Use tokenization or redaction when needed.
- Backups: daily snapshot for critical systems; retention per table below.

Retention table
| Data class | Minimum retention | Archival/storage location |
|------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| Public | 90 days | General buckets |
| Internal | 1 year | Company buckets |
| Confidential | 7 years | Encrypted, access-controlled storage |
| Restricted | As contract/regulation | Encrypted, restricted-region storage |

Data access and sharing
- Data access requests follow the Access & Permissions process and require a documented business justification.
- Cross-team sharing requires a data use agreement (DUA) for Confidential/Restricted data.
- External transfers must be approved by Legal + Security and logged in the Data Transfer register.

Incident handling
- Data incidents reported to security@redwood.com immediately.
- Follow the Incident Response playbook (link in related_pages) and notify Legal for potential breach obligations.

4) Procurement & expenses

Principles and delegations
- Decentralized requests with delegated approval thresholds to balance speed and control.
- Owner: Finance & Procurement (partnered with People Ops for headcount-related spend).

Approval thresholds (summary)
- Expense reimbursements (employee-paid):
  - <= $500: employee submits with receipts; manager approval.
  - $501- $5,000: requires manager + finance review.
  - > $5,000: requires manager + finance + VP approval.
- Vendor spend / PO commitments:
  - <= $10,000: Manager + Procurement notification.
  - $10,001- $100,000: Manager + Procurement approval + Legal review.
  - > $100,000: Procurement + Legal + CFO approval.

Process (software purchases)
1. Submit Procurement Request form with justification, vendor details, budget code, and anticipated spend.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor (see Vendor Management checklist) and generates PO if approved.
3. Finance processes invoices against PO; record in ERP within 7 business days of invoice receipt.

Expense policy highlights
- Use company card for business expenses where possible.
- Personal expenses are not reimbursable. Exceptions must be pre-approved by manager.
- International travel and high-value items require pre-approval and budget owner sign-off.

5) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist
1. Business justification and owner identified.
2. Security and privacy questionnaire completed for vendors handling Confidential/Restricted data.
3. Contract template reviewed by Legal; include SLAs, data handling, termination rights, audit rights.
4. Procurement issues PO and records vendor in vendor registry.
5. Technical onboarding and least-privilege credentials provided.

Ongoing management
- Quarterly vendor reviews for strategic vendors (> $50k annually).
- Annual security re-assessment for vendors with access to Confidential/Restricted data.
- Contract renewals: Procurement to start renewal process 90 days before expiry.

Offboarding
- Revoke access to systems within 24 hours of contract termination.
- Ensure return or deletion of company data per contract obligations and document completion.

6) Travel policies

Booking and approvals
- All travel must be booked through the company travel portal or approved travel agency.
- Domestic travel: manager approval required.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval; check visa and security advisories.

Allowances and reimbursements
- Per diem: refer to the Travel Per Diem table in the Travel template.
- Flights: economy for <8hr flights; business with VP approval for flights >8hr.
- Hotel: business-class/standard corporate rate; exceptions approved by manager.

Safety and emergency
- Register travel with People Ops for trips to higher-risk regions.
- Emergency contact: people-ops@redwood.com; security on-call for safety incidents.

7) Internal templates and examples

Available templates (canonical copies live in the Templates space):
- Access Request (form): fields for requester, role, resource, justification, duration, manager approval.
- Change Request (CR) template: impact, rollback plan, test plan, schedule, owners.
- Procurement Request / PO template: vendor, budget code, justification, cost breakdown.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: standard 3rd-party security profile + required evidence checklist.
- Expense Reimbursement form: expense type, date, receipts, manager approval.
- Travel Request template: itinerary, business purpose, approvals, emergency contacts.

How to use templates
1. Copy the canonical template and fill all required fields.
2. Attach supporting documentation (quotes, test results, approvals).
3. Submit to the appropriate queue (Access, Change Board, Procurement, Finance).

Audit, exceptions, and enforcement
- Exceptions: must be submitted with justification and an owner; exceptions expire after 90 days unless renewed.
- Audits: periodic internal audits by Finance, Security, and People Ops to ensure compliance.
- Non-compliance: may result in revocation of access, denial of reimbursements, or disciplinary action depending on severity.

Appendix: Quick links and contacts
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.com, finance@redwood.com
- Security: security-team@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com
- Change Board: change-board@redwood.com

Change log
